public_context.environment_introduction:
# Environment Information

## Brief Introduction:  
This environment encompasses a centralized emergency response system used by hospitals and municipal services to manage ambulance dispatch.  
It maintains real-time records of incidents, available ambulances, locations, patient details, and dispatch statuses.  
Operators use the system to quickly allocate resources and communicate with emergency teams, ensuring rapid and accurate responses to medical emergencies like heart attacks.

## Environment Rules / Constraints:  
- An ambulance can only be assigned to one active incident at a time.
- Incidents must have a precise location (address or GPS) to be created.
- Only available ambulances (availability_status = "available") can be dispatched.
- Patient privacy must be protected according to applicable regulations.
- Dispatch status (“requested”, “en route”, “arrived”, “completed”) must be updated based on ambulance progress.
public_context.task: A follow-up caller reports that incident INC1003 (Respiratory Distress for patient PAT004) was mislocated and actually occurred at 201 Elm Street, Midtown (location LOC5). Validate LOC5 for incident use and correct INC1003’s location to LOC5. Then, dispatch the closest available ambulances to both pending incidents INC1003 and INC1005 (Stroke for patient PAT005), prioritizing proximity by GPS/address data and respecting availability and single-assignment constraints. Progress both incidents through the full dispatch lifecycle: set status to “en route” upon assignment, update ambulance availability to “unavailable,” update ambulance current_location as they travel and on arrival, mark incidents “arrived,” then mark them “completed” after resolution. Finally, release the assigned ambulances back to “available” status and apply patient data anonymization for PAT004 and PAT005 so their identifiable information is redacted in subsequent queries/exports.

function.description:
Retrieve patient details (patient_id, age, medical_condition, masked contact_info) by patient name,
while preserving privacy.

Args:
    name (str): Patient name to search for (case-insensitive exact match).

Returns:

        {
            "success": True,
            "data": [
                {
                    "patient_id": str,
                    "age": int,

                    "contact_info": str  # masked for privacy
                },
                ...

            "error": str
        }

Constraints:
    - Patient privacy must be protected: contact_info field is masked for output.

function.description:
Retrieve patient details by their unique patient_id.

Args:
    patient_id (str): The unique identifier of the patient.

Returns:

        "data": PatientInfo     # Patient record details if found

    or

        "error": "Patient not found"

Constraints:

function.description:

Args:
    patient_id (str): Unique identifier for the patient to anonymize.

Returns:
    dict:
        - On success: {
            "success": True,
            "message": "Patient info anonymized for patient_id <patient_id>"
          }
        - On error: {
            "success": False,
            "error": "<reason>"
          }

Constraints:
    - Patient must exist.
    - After anonymization, no PII (name/contact_info) is accessible for that patient.
    - Operation is idempotent (can run multiple times without further effect).
